post.caption: Green powder turns shakudo black. Shakudo means red copper, an alloy with a few percent gold. Its black color appears only after the surface is treated. Makers simmer it in a hot rokusho solution of copper salts. Rokusho itself is a green blue copper powder. Grated daikon radish is part of the traditional process. The finished color is a deep blue black, sometimes purple. Rows of tiny punched domes, called nanako, give a fish roe texture. It decorated sword fittings such as guards and grip ornaments. After 1876, Meiji makers turned shakudo fittings into small jewelry.
